newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- MAY 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- MAY 5.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Revelations from the papers of veteran statesman Constantine Karamanlis that the former king of Greece was planning a coup as late as 1975 has caused a furore in Greece and is causing grief to pro-royalists in the conservative opposition New Democracy party which Karamanlis founded and led and is now led by his nephew.

--Funds for pensions are drying up, Bank of Greece Governor Lucas Papademos warns. "Employer contributions in the future will be even less sufficient than today to cover the disbursal of pensions," Papademos says. Pension funds deficits are expected to hit the one trillion drachma mark in 1996.
--Britain's Labour government has refused to meet its promise to return the Elgin Marbles.
--A new civil servants' code that is expected to radically change the status quo in the public service is expected to come to light within the next few days.
--Retroactive payments and increases will be included in pension cheques delivered in May: the increases range from 2.1 to 8.0 percent.
